body: The U.N. convention and seabed claims have been in the spotlight recently as interest grows in seabed mining for critical minerals
to drive conflict over Arctic shelf claims
— over 200 nautical miles from any coast —
for resource extraction. The Arctic Ocean still freezes in the winter
The seabed mining industry, like most global industry, is likely to look for
less costly options in warmer latitudes

While it cannot be assumed that Russia will continue pursuing its shelf claims in accordance with international law, it is likely to use lower-cost tools like lawfare or information warfare to complicate central Arctic Ocean claims, rather than apply high-cost and hard-to-sustain military options.
